headline: Oil's 7% plunge lifts the Dow, but Oracle and chip selling drag the Nasdaq down 1.1%
summary: A rebound that faded into a split close. Stocks opened higher on US-Iran peace hopes, with the S&P 500 up as much as 1.1% in the morning, but selling in tech and chip stocks built through the afternoon and the index closed on its session low. Most stocks still rose: consumer discretionary, financials, industrials and staples gained as oil and yields fell, while tech lost close to 3% and energy about 4%.
drivers: Chip selling resumes after a brief bounce

The SOX gave up an early gain of almost 2% to close 3.4% lower, extending Friday's 7.2% slide. Marvell fell about 13% and Lumentum about 19% after agreeing a $115 billion all-stock merger that analysts questioned on size, while Intel dropped another 8.8% after Friday's 29% plunge.
AI funding worries hit Oracle and software

Oracle sank about 8.7% after filings showed plans to raise $20 billion through stock and bond sales, feeding concern over how AI build-outs are being financed. Microsoft (−2.8%) and Apple (−1.8%, ahead of its report) were among the heaviest weights on the S&P 500.

WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46, back below $100, and Brent 7.6% to $104.77 after Iran said its supreme leader had widened the mandate for peace talks and President Trump said a deal could happen. Airlines, cruise lines and retailers rallied while Exxon and other energy names fell about 4%.
Lower yields support cyclicals and the Dow

The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.92% as oil fell, helping home-improvement, financial and industrial stocks; Honeywell, 3M and Boeing led the Dow's 0.4% gain. October ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5, above forecasts, with the prices-paid gauge easing.
week: The week opened with the Dow up 0.4% and the S&P 500 down 0.5% after the Nasdaq's 5.3% October drop, its worst month since March 2025; the backdrop is a Fed on hold at 3.75–4%, a 10-year yield back under 5% and oil swinging on Iran headlines.
watch: Next: after Monday's close Apple reported revenue of $114.5 billion and EPS of $2.10, both above forecasts; Tuesday brings the midterm elections, JOLTS job openings and AMD's results, followed by Arm and Qualcomm on Wednesday and the October jobs report on Friday, Nov 6.
